messages:
mira: Quick intake for a new onboarding — falconx-xl-14b (community fork). Need a prioritized perf/quant bring-up and a small runbook for gating. TL;DR: baseline float16, int8/int4 smoke, batch/ctx sweeps, a tiny quality spot-check set, and a gate for rolling to staging. Proposed checklist below.

mira: Proposed checklist:
- baseline (fp16) throughput/latency w/ batch sweep (1,2,4,8,16) and ctx sweep (512,1024,2048)
- quant smoke (int8, int4) compare latency/throughput + mem
- quality smoke: 200 prompts (mix: QA, summarization, code) run for fp16 vs quant; record EM/F1 and 5-shot QA drift
- regression gate: p95 latency <= 250ms @ batch=1 ctx=1024 on Dedicated (stretch target: <=200ms)
- storage: put raw traces + parsed CSV in /ml/onboard/falconx-xl-14b/bench_results
- signoff: perf owner + QA owner + infra

mira: quick command sketch to use for perf runs (copy/paste):
```bash
python -m bench.run \  --model falconx-xl-14b \  --device cuda:0 \  --batches 1,2,4,8,16 \  --ctxs 512,1024,2048 \  --warmup 50 \  --steps 300 \  --metrics p50,p95,p99,tokens_per_sec,mem_peak
```

javier: I can own the baseline sweeps. prefer to run on a staging Dedicated node (A100-80GB) so mem/throughput numbers are realistic. Thursday morning UTC works for me.

sam: I’ll take quant smoke & quality diffs. For quality set, can we use the small eval harness (200 prompts) from /ml/evals/quick_checks? includes code, summarization, and factual QA. I’ll produce a small report with delta EM/F1 + a few example regressions.

priya: Add an explicit check for KV-cache warmup behavior — some quant builds show wrong early-token latencies. Also add a step to measure cold vs warm p95.

anastasia: Also log batching efficiency curve: tokens/sec per GPU vs batch size and per-request latency breakdown. We should save both raw traces and parsed CSV.

mira: Good. Owners: javier (baseline), sam (quant + quality), priya (cache/regressions), anastasia (tracing/parsing). I’ll coordinate signoff.

sam: Small note on quant flags: use `--quant int8` and `--quant llm-int4` as separate runs. Don’t mix with other pruning flags. Also keep a float32 reference for memory checks.

javier: Scheduling note — we might need to drop sequence length on some steps if allocation fails; fallback plan: run ctx=512 then 1024 and only attempt 2048 if mem_peak < 70GB on A100-80.

ci-bot: perf-bench job queued (job_id=9876) by javier, target node staging-ded-03, ETA ~45m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mira: Great — please paste the final CSV and a 1-paragraph summary in the folder when done. Quick template for the summary: one-line status (pass/warn/fail), top perf numbers (p50/p95/tokens/s), mem_peak, quant quality delta, follow-up actions.

sam: Quick question — for the regression gate should we use p95 at 99th percentile or p99? My vote: p95 for latency SLA and p99 as a high-severity alert.

priya: Agree with sam. Gate = p95 <= 250ms, alert if p99 > 500ms.

mira: +1. If everyone is good I’ll calendar block Thurs 08:00 UTC for the runs and set a brief signoff meeting 12:00 UTC to review the artifacts. :thumbsup:

anastasia: I’ll add a small parser script to /ml/onboard/falconx-xl-14b/parse_bench.py to normalize CSVs from bench.run.

javier: starting the baseline runs now, will ping here with job link and raw CSV.

ci-bot: perf-bench job started (9876) — logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/9876/logs
